newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic power flat from pre-holiday ranges.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic power flat from pre-holiday ranges.

text.p: Spot prices of wholesale electricity in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. stayed flat Friday from Wednesday's levels in near non-existing activity following the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday.
"There's nothing going on. We're just manning some phones here," an East Coast marketer said.
Almost all Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnect (PJM) utilities, brokers and marketers, as well as the New York Mercantile Exchange, remained closed today.
Spot PJM prices were supported in recent days due to firm natural gas prices and frigid weather in the region.
Temperatures were forecast to rise today after scattered flurries and extreme chill Thursday.
Saturday, temperatures in the midsection of the Atlantic seaboard were predicted to peak in 40s-50s Fahrenheit range and bottom in the 20s-30s.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Saturday was still quoted at $20.00-$20.25 a megawatt hour (MWh), Sunday $18.75-$19.25 and Monday $26.25-$27.00.
Firm, off-peak PJM electricity held steady from Wednesday's level at $12.00-$16.00 for Saturday and Sunday and $13.00-!6.50 for Monday.
December PJM power deliveries remained at $27.50-$28.00.
January/February 1997 PJM electricity was still assessed at $32.80-$33.10.
March 1997 PJM deliveries were notationally talked at $25.50-$25.75, flat from Wednesday's range.
Second-quarter 1997 PJM deliveries held steady at $22.80-$22.90.
The 833 Beaver Valley 2 nuclear power plant was planned to resume service over the weekend after a longer-than-expected outage tied to refueling and repairs.
